rows: Technique, you call it. Again. Interesting. Which version of it did you practise?
Brawling, is it? That is a prettier word than the version I saw.
Risk, you told me. A gamble worth taking is one you can describe twice the same way.
Slow pace. Lovely. Which pace do you mean, the one you announced or the one you use?
The people deserve a straight answer. I think I owe them one.
I know what I said, and I can repeat it exactly.
I am not the one who needs a crowd to tell me my value.
Look at this pose. It says one thing, and I mean exactly that.
You claim technique. Repeat the claim, then show the evidence.
Strikes, you said. Which strike, and when?
You called it a risk. I would call it a gamble with the wrong tone.
Slowing down is a choice. You keep telling people you made it.
The crowd are owed the true version of this, not the flattering one.
You want to be among the best. Repeat that, and then tell me why.
You are proud of your {strength}. I have heard you say it before. I have heard you say it before, and it reads differently now.
I have listened to your {strength} twice. The second time was more interesting.
You stayed level, the second time I noticed. Good, because calm is where I like to ask questions.
Right, that is fair, I noted it. We agree on that, which is rare enough to note.
I could ask you to explain that. I think you would rather not.
One fall, then, the way you said it. Repeat the terms once more, so there is no confusion about them later.
On the mat I will ask one question at a time. Answer each one.
Grounded or standing, I will still be asking the same question.
Stay where you are and answer it properly.
Decent answer. Now say it again, in the ring.
Did you answer? I heard something close to one.
Right, that is fair, I noted it. I shall note that for later.
I take that on board. I will remember you said it.
I will say the same thing at the finish as I have said here.
My approach is careful. I do not repeat myself unless I mean it.
Whatever happens, the record will be correct.
The question is not closed. Only the bell will close it.
I have one more question, and you will answer it when the bell goes.
If you asked me to repeat the charge and explain it, I couldn't give you a specific example that proves it. I won't repeat it.
I've listened to your question. There isn't enough behind my accusation for me to stand by it.
Noted. We can leave the allegation out of the discussion from now on.
That's the answer I was asking for. Let's find out what the wrestling tells us.
Repeat what you intend to prove, then let the crowd compare it with what you actually do.
Which version shall we judge? I suggest the one that happens in the ring, where everybody can see it.
